extracted.intended_audience: Users of the TikZ/PGF packages — LaTeX/TeX authors and technical users creating graphics and diagrams with TikZ/PGF
extracted.subtask_description: Producing vector graphics and diagrams inside TeX documents using the TikZ/PGF package; covers tutorials, design principles, syntax, libraries, and guidelines for good graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning the Time Needed for the Creation of Graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan and estimate the time required to create a graphic (section heading: "Planning the Time Needed for the Creation of Graphics").

rubrics_metrics.name: Workflow for Creating a Graphic
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow a defined workflow when creating graphics (section heading: "Workﬂow for Creating a Graphic").

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking Graphics With the Main Text
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure graphics are properly linked, referenced, and integrated with the main body text (section heading: "Linking Graphics With the Main Text").

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency Between Graphics and Text
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain consistency of style, notation, and terminology between graphics and the surrounding text (section heading: "Consistency Between Graphics and Text").

rubrics_metrics.name: Labels in Graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and place labels in graphics so they are readable, unambiguous, and consistent (section heading: "Labels in Graphics").

rubrics_metrics.name: Plots and Charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance specific to creating plots and charts (section heading: "Plots and Charts").

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention and Distraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage visual emphasis so graphics attract attention to important elements without causing distraction (section heading: "Attention and Distraction").

rubrics_metrics.name: Design Principles: TikZ ist kein Zeichenprogramm
rubrics_metrics.description: High-level design philosophy ("TikZ ist kein Zeichenprogramm" / TikZ is not a drawing program) — the package is a programmable graphics system with design consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Syntax For Specifying Points
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the special point-specifying syntax provided by PGF/TikZ when defining coordinates (section heading: "Special Syntax For Specifying Points").

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Syntax For Path Specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the prescribed syntax for path construction and specification (section heading: "Special Syntax For Path Speciﬁcations").

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions on Paths
rubrics_metrics.description: When using paths, select appropriate actions (draw, fill, clip, shade, etc.) and associated parameters (section heading: "Actions on Paths").

rubrics_metrics.name: Key-Value Syntax for Graphic Parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the key–value parameter syntax for specifying graphic options and styles (section heading: "Key-Value Syntax for Graphic Parameters").

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Syntax for Specifying Nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use TikZ's node-specifying syntax and options to create and configure nodes (section heading: "Special Syntax for Specifying Nodes").

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Syntax for Specifying Trees
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the tree/child syntax and options when constructing hierarchical/tree diagrams (section heading: "Special Syntax for Specifying Trees").

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of Graphic Parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Group graphic parameters for modularity and readability (section heading: "Grouping of Graphic Parameters").

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate Transformation System
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand and use the coordinate transformation system (canvas vs. coordinate transforms) to place and transform graphic elements (section heading: "Coordinate Transformation System").

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Scopes to Structure a Picture
rubrics_metrics.description: Use scopes to localize transformations and parameters and to structure complex pictures (section heading: "Using Scopes to Structure a Picture").

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Styles to Manage How Pictures Look
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and apply styles to manage consistent appearance across nodes, paths, and entire pictures (section heading: "Using Styles to Manage How Pictures Look").

rubrics_metrics.name: When Should One Use TikZ for Generating Plots?
rubrics_metrics.description: Guideline on when it is appropriate to use TikZ (PGF) itself to generate plots versus using other tools (section heading: "When Should One Use TikZ for Generating Plots?").

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency and Accuracy of the Mathematical Engine
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and usage considerations for the mathematical engine, including its efficiency and numerical accuracy (section heading: "Eﬃciency and Accuracy of the Mathematical Engine").

rubrics_metrics.name: Commands for Parsing and Evaluating Mathematical Expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the provided commands and syntax for parsing and evaluating mathematical expressions inside TikZ/PGF (section heading: "Commands for Parsing Expressions" / "Syntax for mathematical expressions").

rubrics_metrics.name: Plotting Best Practices: Plot Path Operation and Plotting Functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on plotting: using the plot path operation, when to read points from files, plotting functions and using gnuplot, placing marks, and choosing plot types (sections under "Plots of Functions" including "The Plot Path Operation", "Plotting a Function", "Plotting a Function Using Gnuplot", "Placing Marks on the Plot", "Smooth Plots, Sharp Plots, and Comb Plots").

rubrics_metrics.name: Path-Centered Approach and Coordinate Versus Canvas Transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: Architectural/design guidance: favor a path-centered approach and understand the difference between coordinate and canvas transformations when designing the package and constructing graphics (section headings: "Path-Centered Approach" and "Coordinate Versus Canvas Transformations").
